q: How fit do I need to be?
a: You need reasonable fitness, but the trips are not endurance tests. Each trip carries a rating from 1 to 5 built from climate, terrain, vegetation, hours walked and pack weight. Someone who has never walked off track should rate each walk one level harder than shown. A positive mental attitude matters more than being superfit.

q: Is any of the walking on marked trails?
a: Almost none. The guides lead you off the trail into places that can only be reached on foot. The Kakadu Day Walks and the accommodated sections of a few trips are the exceptions.

On every trip you carry a pack with your food and equipment. Pack weights are shown on each trip: 8 to 12 kg on the easier trips, 12 to 15 kg on most, 15 to 18 kg on the long circles. Day walk trips need a day pack only. On many trips there are days at a base camp where you walk without your pack.
Four to twelve walkers plus one or more guides. All trips need at least four or five bookings to be a definite departure, and no trip is 100 percent definite more than 60 days before departure.

There is no month in Kakadu or the Kimberley where most days do not reach 30 degrees. The wet season, December to April, is a time of waterfalls and wildflowers and warm rain. The dry season, April to September, brings clear skies and weather so reliable that few people carry tents. The Build Up, September to December, is the most dramatic season of all. The Red Centre and Pilbara are neither as hot nor as humid for most of the year. Everyone benefits from a bit of acclimatisation.

q: What is a wet season trip like?
a: You are going to get wet, and most people simply accept that. It will be hot, humid and somewhat physically challenging. Waterfalls flow everywhere and you have most places to yourself. A pack liner is essential, leather boots are not recommended, and a light poncho or a small umbrella beats a raincoat. Read the wet season page before booking any trip from Christmas through March.

q: What happens if things go wrong?
a: Accidents don't happen often, but they do happen. Every major expedition carries a satellite phone and a backup EPIRB. Help would be some hours away, as it would be on a remote rural road. Since 1986 Mother Nature has thrown up a few challenges, far fewer than most people expect, and the trips have coped.

Request a place on the trip page, or send the booking form, and the office confirms by email. No booking is confirmed until the booking form and a 50 deposit are in and the trip registration and liability release is returned. Full payment is due 60 days before departure, or earlier to take an advance purchase discount.

Book and pay four months ahead for 20 percent off, three months for 15, two months for 10. Past clients take a further 5 percent, members of the ACF, Wilderness Society, NPA of NSW, VNPA or YHA 5 percent, groups of five 5 percent and groups of ten 10 percent. Up to three discounts, maximum 35 percent, applied one after the other. Consecutive sections of one trip save 10 per extra section. The discounts do not apply to the international trips.

Cancel in writing. More than 60 days before departure you lose the 50 deposit; 36 to 60 days, 25 percent of the tour cost; 29 to 35 days, 50 percent; 21 to 28 days, 75 percent; less than 21 days, no refund. If Willis's Walkabouts cancels a trip, all fees paid are refunded, with at least five weeks notice where possible.

It is strongly recommended, and it should cover emergency evacuation and cancellation fees. Some evacuations are not covered by medical or ambulance insurance and could cost more than 000. Participants are liable for their own evacuation costs.

Unless a trip says otherwise, transport on all complete trips is from and to Darwin, Kununurra, Alice Springs or Tom Price. There is an important pre trip meeting the evening before departure. Trips normally leave about 8 am in the Northern Territory and earlier in Western Australia, with pick up from your accommodation. Never schedule flights on the day a trip or section begins or ends without checking first.

q: Can I do just part of a long trip?
a: Yes. Most of the longer trips are divided into sections that can be done on their own, each with its own price. Those doing one section find their own way to or from the connection point, which always has a bus service. Details are in the trip notes.

q: Can I bring my own vehicle?
a: On any trip using self drive hire vehicles you may provide your own transport, usually a four wheel drive, and receive a discount of 0 to over 00 depending on distance and passengers.
